title: Agent Interoperability Protocols (A2A / ACP)
abstract: The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol and its predecessor ACP (Agent Communication Protocol) define how AI agents discover, communicate, and collaborate with each other — complementing MCP which handles agent-to-tool communication.

title: AG-UI — Agent-User Interaction Protocol
abstract: AG-UI (Agent-User Interaction Protocol) by CopilotKit defines how AI agents stream rich output to frontend applications — streaming chat, generative UI, shared state, human-in-the-loop interactions, and tool rendering. It complements MCP (agent↔tools) and A2A (agent↔agent) as the agent↔user layer.

title: AI-DLC — AI-Driven Development Life Cycle
abstract: AI-DLC is an AI-centric methodology by AWS that reimagines the entire software development lifecycle. Rather than retrofitting AI as an assistant into existing SDLC processes, AI-DLC positions AI as a central collaborator throughout three phases — Inception (requirements via 'Mob Elaboration'), Construction (architecture and code via 'Mob Construction'), and Operations (deployment with oversight). It replaces sprints with 'bolts' (hours/days), epics with 'units of work', and emphasises human-in-the-loop oversight at every step.

title: AGENTS.md — Open Standard for AI Coding Agents
abstract: AGENTS.md is an emerging open standard for declaring AI agent capabilities, tools, and instructions in a structured markdown file at the root of a repository, enabling consistent agent discovery and interoperability across platforms.
